messages:
tony: Heads up — planning a preflight maintenance window for AZ21 GPU pool tonight 00:30–02:30 UTC. Purpose: soft-evac + QoS "shadow" backfill to seed KV/prefix caches and warm batching paths before the kernel/nic microcode patch tomorrow. Expect transient task reschedules but no hard downtime for most tenants.

infra-oncall: Can you summarize capacity impact and canaries?

ton y: Canaries: 2-node canary at 00:30 (cohort-canary). Roll cohorts every ~10m, 20 nodes per cohort after canary. Backfill will temporarily reserve ~8–12% of total pool for warm tasks (kv_seed + batch-warmers) for up to 90m. Estimated tail-latency risk window ~5–15m per cohort during warm.

maya: We have an enterprise job starting at 01:00 UTC (priority-tenant-3). Can we scope this to avoid impact?

ton y: Yes — priority-tenant-3 stays pinned to pool-az21-hot (no preemption). We'll mark them with `no-evac=true`. All non-critical jobs will be preemptible. Command we'll run to pin: 
```
rbctl tenancy update --tenant priority-tenant-3 --pool pool-az21-hot --no-evac true
```

jasper: If we reserve 8–12% for backfill, do we have room for burst traffic? Any auto-backfill->spot fallback?

ton y: Autoscale still active. If we see persistent tail above thresholds we'll throttle backfill rate. Backfill job supports rate-limits. Fallback policy: route latency-sensitive requests to rtx-variant model nodes (lower throughput, higher cost) automatically.

sasha: What's the exact kv seeding command and where will metrics be pushed? I want to hook our dashboards and set alarms.

ton y: kv_seed lives in ops-runner, we'll run it as a job with tags. Example: 
```
ops-runner run kv_seed --prefix az21 --workers 120 --rate 500 --ttl 90m --tag maintenance_7473210987
```
Metrics: push to `infra.metrics.kv_seed.{success,qps,latency}` and `infra.latency.tokens` — watch 95th and 99th pct. Dashboards: /dash/az21-backfill and /dash/token-slo.

infra-oncall: Rollback plan? If latencies spike above 2x SLO for >5m for priority tenants we abort backfill and uncordon nodes. What are the exact commands?

ton y: Rollback steps: 1) run `ops-runner cancel maintenance_7473210987` to stop kv_seed and warmers. 2) run `rbctl uncordon --cohort <active-cohort>` to return nodes. 3) failover routing: `routerctl set-route --pool pool-az21-hot --fallback rtx-variant` (this is automatic if abort triggers).

deploy-bot: :robot_face: maintenance job created: `maintenance-7473210987` scheduled 2026-03-22T00:30:00Z · canary=2nodes · cohorts=~20nodes/10m · tags=[az21,preflight,qos-backfill]

maya: Asking to postpone by 1 hour is not possible — customer cannot move. Can we instead reduce backfill rate to 200 qps and extend window?

ton y: We can do that. Lowering rate to 200 qps increases warm time; we'll extend TTL to 140m for buffers. New cmd: 
```
ops-runner run kv_seed --prefix az21 --workers 80 --rate 200 --ttl 140m --tag maintenance_7473210987
```
We'll prioritize no-evac tenants and monitor SLOs closely.

jasper: Cost hit estimate for reducing rate (longer runtime)?

ton y: Rough ballpark: original plan ~2.1 GPU-hours of extra work across pool; reduced rate raises that to ~3.4 GPU-hours — ~$60 additional for tonight. Not material vs potential 99th pct penalties.

infra-oncall: I'll stand up the watch and paging for 00:20–03:00 UTC. I'll also add transient-alerts: infra.latency.tokens.p99 > 1.8x baseline for 5m -> page.

sasha: I'll add a dashboard panel for kv_seed qps and a log filter for `maintenance_7473210987` in the next 5m.

ton y: thanks — please ack if you're good. :thumbsup:

maya: ack :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: ack.

sasha: ack (will post dashboard link once ready).
